scope: Initial source-backed inventory for workspace/session, worklanes/panes, command routing, and coding agents required by issue 7.

entries.behavior: Decode, migrate, preserve, and export ordered schema-v3 windows, worklanes, columns, panes, selections, frames, titles, CWDs, commands, colors, and bookmark origins.
entries.user_impact: Without exact recipes, Linux cannot restore the workspace users created in Zentty.
entries.test_plan: Focused fixtures cover unversioned, explicit source-v2, schema-v3, future-compatible, color, title, CWD, command, and meaningful-default contracts. Controlled X11 and Wayland staged-product journeys import source-compatible recipes, mutate real GTK topology and divider geometry through physical input, inspect live and clean JSON, relaunch real Ghostty PTYs, and prove exact identities/topology with pixel-equivalent persisted proportions.

entries.behavior: Atomically save debounced live snapshots and synchronous clean-exit snapshots while rejecting stale generations and filtering meaningless defaults.
entries.user_impact: Workspace changes would otherwise disappear at ordinary shutdown or race into an older snapshot.
entries.test_plan: Focused store tests prove atomic replacement, stale-generation rejection, meaningful-default filtering, corrupt fallback, and save-reason policy. Controlled X11 and Wayland actors drive real GTK changes, honor the owned 350 ms debounce, inspect live and synchronous clean-exit envelopes, and relaunch the resulting real workspace.

entries.behavior: Use the lifecycle marker to distinguish clean restore preference from mandatory crash recovery, consume successful restores, and report unusable snapshots.
entries.user_impact: A crash would lose all current worklanes or repeatedly relaunch a corrupt snapshot.
entries.test_plan: The staged product mutates topology through real GTK input, waits for the asynchronous 350 ms live snapshot, dies by SIGKILL, relaunches on both controlled X11 and Wayland with normal restoration disabled, restores exact real Ghostty/PTTY topology, consumes the prepared snapshot, and replaces corrupt bytes after reporting a fresh-workspace fallback.

entries.behavior: Create, select, remove, reorder, and keyboard-navigate ordered worklanes while preserving stable identities and active selection.
entries.user_impact: Worklanes are Zentty's primary unit of parallel coding work.
entries.test_plan: Controlled product journeys preserve real menu/action, keyboard and pointer reorder routes, stable identity, active selection, overflow, automatic reveal, contextual transfer, and persisted-order relaunch. The actual GTK worklane selector and selected state are checked with GTK's test backend, then a separate Rust inspector verifies the same staged-product nodes and live topology changes through private real AT-SPI sessions on controlled X11 and Wayland.

entries.behavior: Show and edit optional worklane titles and colors using source trimming, empty-name, menu, and visual treatment behavior.
entries.user_impact: Users cannot distinguish concurrent tasks reliably without durable names and color cues.
entries.test_plan: Keep the existing real GTK modal Save, Cancel, empty-title, color treatment, persisted recipe, and accessibility journeys green. Add focused catalog coverage and a real menu journey proving that Move Pane destinations use current custom worklane titles, update immediately after rename, disambiguate duplicate titles, and retain stable destination identity.

entries.behavior: Render compound worklane cards with nested pane summaries, current context, progress, review state, and human-attention state.
entries.user_impact: A terminal list without status and attention loses the at-a-glance coding-agent workflow that defines Zentty.
entries.test_plan: Authenticated real agent events exercise running, progress, needs-input, failure, completion, and clearing in the staged product. The actual GTK pane/worklane nodes are separately checked for source-derived accessible labels and selected state on controlled X11 and Wayland.

entries.behavior: Represent ordered columns and vertical panes; split, focus, resize, arrange, and move panes within and across worklanes according to PaneCommand semantics.
entries.user_impact: The structural port now provides Add Pane Left, directional focus, all source width/height arrangement presets, golden focus ratios, reset layout, stable reflow, contextual move UI, accessible pointer/arrow-key divider resizing, persisted real-terminal geometry, and all four source cell-based keyboard resize commands. Cross-window moves remain incomplete.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland journeys physically drag both divider axes, equalize with double-click, preserve exact geometry across relaunch, transfer live real Ghostty PTYs within and across windows/worklanes, and retain focus. Core tests prove directional and arrangement semantics; the actual divider widget is checked as a focusable named separator with a nonempty accessible label.

entries.behavior: Close panes with source focus fallback and restore recently closed panes with CWD and command context.
entries.user_impact: Undo Close Pane restores a recent user-closed local pane with a fresh identity, original slot/weight, custom title, real Ghostty surface, focus, and persistence. It preserves real terminal output in an expiring XDG archive, restores validated agent resume context ahead of the previous command, falls back from a deleted CWD to its nearest existing ancestor or home, presents a visible warning, and rolls the complete restore transaction back if surface construction fails.
entries.test_plan: Core tests cover LIFO/expiry, running/exited and active/inactive close sources, focus fallback, child-exit non-capture, agent-resume precedence, missing-CWD ancestor/home resolution, scrollback composition, and rollback/retry. Controlled X11/Wayland coverage closes and restores a real Ghostty PTY through physical GTK input and asserts real scrollback archival, missing-CWD warning, delivered agent wrapper/resume, fresh identity and PTY, CWD, focus, geometry, persistence, one-model/one-surface/one-child ownership, and callback quiescence. Debug single- and multi-terminal Valgrind cells exercise the same product ownership paths with reviewed suppressions; ReleaseSafe remains an explicit executable XFAIL.

entries.behavior: Preserve pane working directory, launch and last-run command, custom title, remembered title, and last-activity title using source normalization rules.
entries.user_impact: Restored terminals would open in the wrong project or lose the context that identifies their task.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland source-recipe journeys launch real shells in controlled temporary directories, prove stored CWD and command metadata, preserve custom and remembered title fields through clean/crash snapshots, relaunch real Ghostty PTYs, and route fresh input to the restored selected pane.

entries.behavior: Drag panes and worklanes with source hit testing, split zones, insertion feedback, and cross-worklane outcomes.
entries.user_impact: Direct spatial manipulation is available alongside named move actions, including live cross-window transfer.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland use real pointer-driven GTK drag/drop against actual pane and sidebar widgets, including source hit testing, rendered insertion feedback, same-window moves, cross-worklane moves, and cross-window live Ghostty surface/PTY transfer without process recreation.

entries.behavior: Expose Ghostty-backed pane search through the pane search HUD and command routing.
entries.user_impact: Long coding and agent transcripts are impractical to navigate without terminal search.
entries.test_plan: Physical X11 covers search, navigation, selection-to-find, typed-query hide-with-remembered-highlights, selection-query close-and-clear, live-query/corner retention, and PTY focus. Controlled Wayland covers the real Ghostty core and named routes; the later source-UX visual closeout adds reviewed light/dark/scaled search HUD evidence without converting unavailable headless-Weston virtual-keyboard injection into a pass.

entries.behavior: Resolve and execute command-palette results through the same availability and action-routing paths as menus and shortcuts.
entries.user_impact: Many Zentty workflows would be present but undiscoverable or unreachable on Linux.
entries.test_plan: Port deterministic result resolution, then open the real palette and invoke worklane, pane, and agent commands through named GTK actions.

entries.behavior: Provide Linux-native GTK actions, accelerators, context menus, and accessible names for source commands without copying AppKit menu implementation details.
entries.user_impact: Linux desktop users need native discoverability, keyboard routing, and accessibility rather than AppKit-specific menu objects.
entries.test_plan: The closed source command inventory maps commands to named GTK actions, accelerators, popovers, and pane-local controls. Real pointer/keyboard journeys remain authoritative for routing; the GTK test backend checks widget contracts, and a separate Rust AT-SPI process verifies externally exposed roles, labels, states, actions, exact product identity, focus, and a real Add Pane Right topology change on X11 and Wayland.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: GTK4 actions, accelerators, popovers, and Linux accessibility APIs replace AppKit menus and key equivalents.

entries.behavior: Preserve Ghostty rendering, VT and terminal ownership while shipping Zentty's compatible Ghostty defaults, terminfo, themes, resource lookup, and configuration reload without a second emulator or PTY owner.
entries.user_impact: Every higher-level Zentty workflow depends on ordinary terminal applications rendering and behaving exactly as real Ghostty terminals rather than a partial replacement.
entries.test_plan: Run real Ghostty surfaces and PTYs, validate packaged terminfo/themes/config lookup and live configuration reload, and retain focused ABI/input/lifecycle tests beneath those product scenarios. The optional performance overlay is separately classified as diagnostics.task-terminal-performance and is not folded into this terminal-foundation claim.

entries.behavior: Support physical and composed keyboard input, modifier/layout changes, mouse reporting, selection, clipboard ownership, URL and file drag/drop, middle-click selection paste, selection autoscroll, smooth scrolling, and stable background scrollback.
entries.user_impact: Agent-aware UI is unusable if shells, editors, pagers, multiplexers, selection, or scrolling are subtly damaged by the host application.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland journeys drive primary-selection middle-click paste into a real PTY; a separate GTK URI-list drag into local and real-SSH panes; ordinary vertical scrollback selection; selection edge-drag autoscroll; exact background-viewport continuity; and horizontal pane-switch gestures. Runtime-layout cells keep one physical key position while changing US to German to an explicit remap. Repeat cells capture server/compositor repeat configuration, prove ordered modifier release, transfer focus while a physical key remains down, bound both panes' exact PTY receipts, and prove key-up stops delivery. Separate X11 and Wayland IME cells drive both the packaged Cangjie5 IBus engine and fcitx5 Cangjie5 through physical compositor events, then assert exact non-ASCII PTY commits, explicit preedit cancellation, cross-surface focus ownership, and active-preedit pane destruction. Both fcitx cells use the source-locked upstream GTK4 module version 5.1.7 as the single reviewed support contract because Ubuntu 24.04's 5.1.1 module has an independently reproduced Wayland destruction defect; the product never replaces the host module. Controlled labwc journeys move staged ReleaseSafe and Debug products through 1x, 1.5x, and 2x outputs, checking compositor fractional-scale/viewport events, real Ghostty CSI geometry, split-pane PTYs, SIGWINCH, and SGR pointer coordinates without GDK overrides. Xwayland runs the same staged products through GTK's X11 backend on a process-group-owned Xwayland server, observes compositor and RANDR geometry, proves stable cell metrics without DPI double application, and checks the same PTY and pointer semantics. GH8 is closed and all native input, IME, resize, and scaling cells pass; platform clipboard, search, restore, and remote-transfer cells cover ownership, multiple windows, hidden panes, and hostile transfer cases.

entries.behavior: Route Backspace through the active GTK IME preedit so composition is edited or cancelled without leaking a terminal key event, corrupting committed text, or transferring composition to another pane.
entries.user_impact: Users of composed-input languages can corrupt the preedit or send an unintended Backspace to the shell when correcting text.
entries.test_plan: Add a focused GTK input-context contract and extend the real nested X11 and Wayland IBus/fcitx journeys to create an active non-ASCII preedit, press physical Backspace, verify the compositor-driven preedit update or cancellation, then commit and assert exact PTY bytes. Retain cross-surface focus and pane-destruction counterexamples; environmental absence must remain non-passing.

entries.behavior: Recognize SSH pane identity, show a remote marker, and safely upload pasted or dropped local files/images to the resolved remote host before inserting the escaped remote path.
entries.user_impact: Remote users otherwise receive misleading local paths or lose Zentty's source workflow for moving images and files into an SSH session.
entries.test_plan: Real X11 and input-capable Wayland journeys paste desktop file-list and PNG clipboard content into a live remote Ghostty pane, transfer through disposable OpenSSH, compare remote bytes/signature, insert the verified path, submit it to the remote actor, and return to the same local PTY. Both compositors reject a symlink as the second member of a two-file paste and prove rollback of the first published final with no insertion. Both also hold a real SCP after remote partial allocation, exit the SSH foreground process, and prove identity-driven cancellation, no insertion, partial cleanup, and local-PTY continuation. X11 and a separate controlled multi-window Weston/Wayland mode both drive a physical cross-process drag from a real GTK URI-list source into the Ghostty widget and verify the remote checksum. The standalone real-SSH actor proves SCP, collision rejection, and the narrowly classified no-SFTP stream fallback.

entries.behavior: Capture, persist, edit, update, import/export, unlink, and restore reusable bookmark and preset workspace shapes including topology, proportions, paths, titles, colors, live commands, launch targets, and supported agent context.
entries.user_impact: Bookmarks are the source feature for intentionally reusable setups; ordinary crash/session restore does not replace them.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland physically save through the source shortcut, inspect the private XDG file and ambient-secret boundary, quit, restart, activate through the real GTK popover, assert a real Ghostty PTY/CWD/command and recency, then make the stored CWD/command stale and assert fallback CWD, prefilled command, and a visible warning. Both compositors also drive the complete management surface and a real in-process native chooser export/delete/import round trip, validating the portable file and persisted result.

entries.behavior: Create and restore multiple windows and transfer a live pane across worklanes/windows or into a new window without recreating its Ghostty surface, PTY, process, scrollback, title, CWD, or dimensions.
entries.user_impact: Source workflows reorganize live long-running agents and shells across windows; replacement sessions would destroy the state being organized.
entries.test_plan: New-window, existing-foreign-worklane, and real cross-window drag/drop transfers pass controlled Wayland/X11 proof of unchanged PTY PID sets, one Ghostty surface construction, post-move physical input, canonical agent/tmux routing, source-window cleanup, aggregate persistence, and clean/crash relaunch where applicable.

entries.behavior: Hold to open the live Worklane Peek overview, navigate neighboring lanes by keyboard, click and spatial swipe, show project and attention context, shield terminal input, and focus the chosen lane in the active window.
entries.user_impact: Worklane Peek is Zentty's fast visual context switcher and a major part of the worklane UX, not decorative animation.
entries.test_plan: Physical X11 retains the source Tab-duration contract, repeated traversal, spatial arrows, real horizontal wheel, Escape, Control-release, input shielding, exact-card click and focus restoration. The same staged-product journey proves five inactive real Ghostty surfaces stay mapped while live PTY titles plus authenticated agent progress and attention update an open multiworklane Peek, and retains four terminal-text-masked screenshot receipts. Controlled X11 and input-capable Wayland prove project icon projection and physical motion routes; X11 additionally proves GTK reduced motion and real two-window deactivation cancellation. Pure source-pinned tests own precision Surface threshold, axis lock, cancellation, once-per-gesture and natural direction because the controlled compositors expose wheel/virtual-keyboard input but no virtual precision-touchpad device. Real GTK accessibility trees pass on both display backends.

entries.behavior: Reproduce source-accurate icon chrome and hierarchical sidebar controls, rows, badges, context menus, tooltips, accessible names, resize and pinned/overlay visibility rather than retaining developer text-button scaffolding.
entries.user_impact: The source interaction model and information hierarchy are core product behavior; a toolbar of text actions is not Zentty UX.
entries.test_plan: Persisted bounded width and visibility, overlay motion, controlled Wayland pointer resize, Global Find retention, live multiwindow reload, crash restoration, physical focus, source-annotated visual states, and deterministic scaling receipts are covered by maintained product actors. A separate Rust inspector verifies the staged application's real external AT-SPI root, window, worklane, pane controls, selected/focused states, actions, and live pane topology on private X11 and Wayland accessibility sessions.

entries.behavior: Maintain back/forward navigation, recent pane and recent command history, and exact-pane routing from attention, search, menu/fleet and palette actions across windows.
entries.user_impact: High-pane-count workflows need reversible navigation and direct return to recently used or attention-requesting work.
entries.test_plan: Preserve the delivered browser-style Back/Forward stacks, recent-pane and source-eligible session-scoped Recent Actions, accessible palette grouping, exact stable-identity pane routing, hidden-column reveal, worklane traversal, and cross-window attention/fleet activation. Core tests and mutation pin ordering, capacity, eligibility, stale pruning, and deduplication; controlled X11 and Wayland journeys use physical input and real PTYs.

entries.behavior: Search pane-local scrollback or globally across every pane in the current window, present aggregate global results in the sidebar, and navigate the exact visible or hidden match without losing terminal context.
entries.user_impact: Searching a single pane cannot replace Zentty's advertised ability to find terminal output across a busy window.
entries.test_plan: Preserve the controlled X11 and input-capable Wayland journey: three real PTYs across two worklanes, source-ordered aggregate totals and cross-worklane navigation, a concurrent second-window query proving coordinator isolation, clear/end focus restoration, pane-local search interoperability, and the pure debounce/frozen-target/stale-target contracts.

entries.behavior: Provide configurable Clean Copy, exact Copy Raw, automatic clean-copy override, URL/path cleanup, and Copy as Markdown while preserving prose, commands, indentation, blank lines, columns, IPv6 and functional URL parameters.
entries.user_impact: Clean Copy is a named public Zentty feature; corruption or omission forces users back to manually repairing terminal output.
entries.test_plan: Preserve source-derived cleanup and bailout goldens plus mutation coverage; in controlled X11 and Wayland, preserve an independent non-text owner when no Ghostty selection exists, select real terminal text through Select All, read the exact primary selection externally, invoke automatic Copy, Copy Raw and Copy as Markdown through the real command palette, read exact standard-clipboard bytes externally, paste cleaned bytes back through the real PTY, and prove distinct selections remain isolated across two real windows. GH-122 must add the current source's terminal-width-aware structured-newline cases before this returns to IMPLEMENTED. The process-level clipboard config snapshot and automatic clean-copy substitution use the single GH-20 settings owner. Remote non-text paste/upload remains owned by its separately qualified GH-17 workflow.

entries.behavior: Resolve worklane repository, branch and remote context, refresh after relevant work, show project icons, associate pull requests, display CI/approval/conflict/age/error state, refresh manually/adaptively, and open the branch or PR remotely.
entries.user_impact: Branch, project and review context are how users distinguish similar agent panes and understand whether work is ready without switching terminals.
entries.test_plan: Preserve real temporary repositories, branches, detached HEADs, nested CWDs, linked-worktree metadata directories and remotes plus the controlled local HTTP forge behind the real gh-compatible subprocess boundary. Drive real X11 and Wayland process, bounded filesystem, authenticated agent-completion, palette refresh, and remote-open actions; assert source-priority badges, tooltip state, validated URLs, one coalesced probe owner, and watcher teardown; mutation-test precedence/parsing. Project icons have canonical-containment, bounded candidate, cache-invalidation, real GTK decode, opt-out, sidebar, chrome, and Worklane Peek evidence on both controlled display backends.

entries.behavior: Discover source-catalog-ordered built-in and custom Open With targets, resolve the focused local pane directory, launch the configured primary or selected Linux file manager/editor/tool, and skip missing targets diagnostically. Source project-file substitution is Xcode-only and therefore has no available Linux target.
entries.user_impact: Opening the active project in an external editor or file manager is a documented daily workflow even though Finder and AppKit launch APIs are macOS-specific.
entries.test_plan: Discover a real controlled `.desktop` directory handler plus a direct custom executable, drive primary and selected actions with physical X11 and Wayland input against the staged product, assert one exact canonical local target, and pin URI encoding, catalog order, primary fallback, config normalization, missing targets, executable validation, duplicate rejection, and no-shell argv in focused Rust tests and mutation testing.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: Implemented with GIO desktop application discovery and direct executable argv; Linux system file-manager and terminal targets replace Finder while macOS-only Xcode project-file substitution remains unavailable by definition.

entries.behavior: Detect and attribute passive, output-reported and container-published development servers to panes/projects, normalize and rank URLs, ignore noisy ports, open the selected server, refresh, and safely stop an owned server process.
entries.user_impact: Agents commonly run alongside servers; Zentty advertises detection/open/control so users can act without hunting ports and process owners.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland use the staged product, real Ghostty PTY, dynamic listeners, authenticated set/list/open/watch IPC, exact preferred/custom/system browser launchers, forged-target rejection, durable ignore/unignore, and owned graceful stop; the controlled Docker cell adds a real dynamically published container. Focused and mutation tests cover URL normalization/output extraction, ranking, port rules, listener attribution, PID reuse, unrelated processes, termination authorization, browser catalog fallback/deduplication, and shell-free launch plans.

entries.behavior: Discover package scripts, Taskfile, just, make, mise and VS Code project tasks and expose safe dynamic run actions with source naming, origin, ordering, CWD and command behavior.
entries.user_impact: Task runners are a named public feature and connect project files to real repeatable terminal work without adding an IDE.
entries.test_plan: Controlled X11 and Wayland materialize every advertised source format in one real project, discover each through the physical command palette, reject a stale snapshot, open a disabled task's exact source through the configured Open With target, and launch VS Code plus make tasks in real Ghostty PTYs with exact CWD/environment/argv receipts. Focused tests and governed mutation cover parsers, quoting, ordering, revalidation, bounded/symlink safety, and local file launch policy.

entries.behavior: Show per-pane root/foreground process identity, CPU history, and memory usage in a themed accessible diagnostics window with bounded Linux sampling and correct process-tree ownership.
entries.user_impact: The Task Manager lets users identify expensive or stuck work by pane without leaving Zentty or guessing from process titles.
entries.test_plan: Keep the controlled X11/Wayland real-PTY journey for CPU, memory, search, expansion, clipboard, focus, close, PID churn, multiwindow behavior, and deliberate absence of a dead Network column. Deferred issue #65 separately owns any future cgroup/container and trustworthy per-pane network accounting; it is not part of this implemented Task Manager claim.

entries.behavior: Provide secure XDG TOML persistence with defaults, validation, partial reload, last-good state, comment/unknown-key preservation where practical, live watch, and symlink-safe atomic writes as the shared authority for separately inventoried settings surfaces.
entries.user_impact: Users need source settings and safe dotfile-friendly persistence; hard-coded behavior or destructive rewrites make the port untrustworthy.
entries.test_plan: Maintain GH-36's closed contract: secure XDG ownership, strict startup plus independently valid live sections, content-safe last-good recovery, coalesced rename, logical/target symlink watching, product/external last-writer outcomes, interrupted-temporary refusal, shared product serialization, file-plus-directory durability, visible settings refresh, no self-write loops, two-window projection, and exact PTY retention. The broader settings epic remains GH-20, but those page-specific gaps do not reopen this implemented configuration authority.

entries.behavior: Make the complete command registry bindable with physical-key recording, pass-through when unbound, conflicts, clear/reset, left/right-hand presets, clickable previews, search/categories, import and export.
entries.user_impact: Keyboard-first and fully bindable commands are defining source behavior, including preserving terminal input when an app action is unbound.
entries.test_plan: Preserve the controlled X11/Wayland real-settings journey for physical recording, conflict replacement, preset/reset, native GTK chooser export/import, source-compatible persistence, restart, active-action interception, and displaced/unbound bytes reaching a real Ghostty PTY. GH-119 must add the current source's Ghostty-compatible preset, exact binding fixture, settings selection, persistence, and real PTY routing before this returns to IMPLEMENTED. The inventory validator must continue proving that every audited source command is present in the Linux bindable registry; Linux additionally exposes its platform fullscreen and minimize commands. Preserve the zero-survivor shortcut-model mutation receipt.

entries.behavior: Treat Settings as a normal independently managed application window, including closing the active Settings toplevel with the platform Close Window shortcut without closing a terminal window or quitting Zentty.
entries.user_impact: A standard close-window command silently failing in Settings makes window ownership feel broken and can route destructive commands to the wrong toplevel.
entries.test_plan: Add a focused action-routing test and a controlled real-GTK journey that opens Settings from a live terminal window, sends physical Ctrl+W while Settings owns focus, proves only Settings closes, proves the PTY and terminal window remain alive, and checks the same command against terminal-window focus and repeated Settings opens.

entries.behavior: Resolve bundled and user Ghostty themes/config, live-reload included files, preserve non-theme settings, preview and select themes, opacity, background images, dark/light/automatic modes, platform blur alternative, seeded colors and OpenCode synchronization.
entries.user_impact: Ghostty themes and polished live appearance are advertised product features; Linux must not regress to an unconfigurable embedded terminal.
entries.test_plan: Preserve the controlled X11/Wayland settings journey for bundled and user theme selection, preview, dark/light/automatic slots, opacity, OpenCode synchronization, sidebar emphasis, physical-key accessibility, persistence, restart, and live Ghostty reload without PTY loss. Preserve the real managed OpenCode launcher journey for private overlay generation, live palette replacement, verified process identity, and SIGUSR2 refresh. Continue config-reload coverage for included files, partial/invalid edits, symlinks, concurrent writes, last-good recovery, and multiwindow projection; keep non-theme Ghostty keys including background-image intact.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: Linux uses GTK dark/light preference and real terminal opacity. Existing Ghostty background-image configuration is preserved rather than duplicated in Zentty settings. There is no portable Linux compositor blur protocol across supported Wayland and X11 environments, so blur is an explicit documented no-blur degradation rather than a silent or compositor-specific claim.

entries.behavior: Deliver agent and pane attention through sidebar/chrome, a local inbox, Linux desktop notifications and configurable sound, include actual question/context, clear stale items, and route every action to the exact window/worklane/pane.
entries.user_impact: Surfacing and jumping to agents that need attention is Zentty's central value proposition and cannot stop at an in-pane badge.
entries.test_plan: The settings/service boundary uses real controlled freedesktop notification and audio services on X11 and Wayland. The attention journey creates two real Zentty windows and Ghostty PTYs, emits authenticated Codex events, proves the three-second debounce and active-pane suppression policy, inspects actual question and source context at the private desktop service, invokes a real D-Bus action across windows, activates a real GTK inbox row on X11 and the shared typed shortcut on Wayland, and proves physical input reaches the exact PTY. Focused reducer tests cover ready and unresolved-stop history, ordering, dismiss, clear, queued-delivery cancellation, stale pane/window scoping, and all interaction fallbacks; targeted mutation testing kills every viable reducer mutant. Fleet, sound, and inhibitor journeys retain their separate real-system coverage.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: The Linux freedesktop service, sound-theme, private custom-audio alternative, source-shaped shared inbox, badge, exact-pane action authority, in-window fleet, StatusNotifierItem integration, and systemd inhibitor are implemented. Dock-specific badges map to in-app and tray attention where the desktop exposes a watcher; the in-window surface remains authoritative when it does not.

entries.behavior: Present waiting, running, idle and progress state for agent panes across all Zentty windows, with priority grouping, exact-pane actions, settings and quit, using an always-available in-window surface plus a tray/status-notifier integration where supported.
entries.user_impact: Cross-window agent visibility is lost if Linux treats the macOS menu-bar implementation as having no user outcome.
entries.test_plan: The controlled journeys populate two real windows and Ghostty PTYs, then prove waiting, running, incomplete/complete progress, compacting, stop-candidate grace, idle, real tracked-PID death, unresolved stop, recovery, session removal, grouped GTK presentation, source priority, malformed typed-target rejection, accessible Settings/Quit footer actions, exact typed routing, and closed-window registry cleanup. A real private D-Bus watcher inspects StatusNotifierItem state, activates the canonical in-window fleet, observes active and needs-attention transitions, verifies watcher-loss fallback, and proves republish plus shutdown name release. X11 proves physical input at the destination PTY. The focused labwc journey requires a real timestamped nested seat plus xdg-activation-v1, proves that the source window obtains a single-use GDK startup credential, and types into the exact destination PTY after cross-toplevel activation.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: The always-available in-window fleet is the baseline on every Linux desktop. Sessions with a StatusNotifierItem watcher additionally receive the same process-wide aggregate through a standard optional desktop item; watcher absence and loss explicitly retain the in-window fallback. Compositors that do not implement xdg-activation-v1 cannot authorize focus transfer and are not used to claim that behavior passed.

entries.behavior: Optionally prevent system sleep while qualifying tracked agents are running and release the Linux inhibitor immediately when work idles, exits, is closed, the setting changes, or Zentty shuts down.
entries.user_impact: Long agent turns can otherwise pause unexpectedly, but an orphaned inhibitor would harm battery and system behavior.
entries.test_plan: Acquire a real desktop/systemd inhibitor from staged Zentty, inspect it across running/idle/exit/close/crash/restart/settings transitions, and mutation-test qualifying-state and lease-release logic.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: Use the desktop portal or systemd-logind inhibitor API instead of macOS power assertions, with explicit capability reporting when neither is available.

entries.behavior: Ship the complete embedded Rust zentty CLI for version and topology discovery, authenticated selection/control, split/grid/layout/pane/worklane/window operations, notifications, server and integration commands with stable aliases, JSON, stdout/stderr and exit codes.
entries.user_impact: Scriptable pane-aware control and hooks are advertised product behavior and the transport used by agent integrations, notifications and teams.
entries.test_plan: Maintain exact source-command closure in the machine-readable CLI contract. Invoke the real staged CLI as a subprocess into a running product over the authenticated Unix socket on controlled X11 and Wayland, validate versioned JSON against schemas and text against reviewed goldens, exercise command families/aliases/selectors/errors against real PTYs and windows, and mutation-test parsing/auth/output dispatch. All 40 source command symbols remain represented, but GH-118 must accept and prove the current parent-level `zentty list --json panes` ordering before this returns to IMPLEMENTED. Downstream agent context persistence remains separately explicit in the GH-46 agent-event contract rather than being misclassified as a CLI gap.

entries.behavior: Inject pane/instance/CLI/hook context and provide Bash, Zsh, Fish and Nushell shell integration for CWD, activity, wrapper PATH and initial CWD without modifying user config or emitting startup/control-sequence noise.
entries.user_impact: CWD, hooks, CLI routing and clean prompts fail if pane shell integration is incomplete or pollutes terminal input/output.
entries.test_plan: Launch real Bash, Zsh, Fish, and Nushell processes in staged real Ghostty panes under controlled X11 and Wayland; capture exact startup bytes and environment, change CWD, nest shells, run management commands, assert authenticated routing metadata and byte-identical user files, and reject missing or unsupported shell prerequisites rather than skipping them.

entries.behavior: Manage new/close/multiwindow, close-pane/worklane/window and quit confirmation based on real work, fullscreen/display placement and clean shutdown without orphaning PTYs, teardown races, or lost required persistence.
entries.user_impact: Users must be protected from accidentally destroying live agent work while normal Linux window/fullscreen/shutdown behavior remains reliable.
entries.test_plan: One pure typed authority evaluates exact pane/worklane/window/application scope from real Ghostty foreground PID, active agent state, and meaningful session history. Existing controlled X11 and Wayland actors cover idle/live work, active/waiting agents, keyboard cancellation/acceptance, stale and duplicate callbacks, WM close, fullscreen, native X11 and request-only Wayland minimize, activation, compositor-owned placement, PTY reaping, persistence/restart, and empty/last-target boundaries without a second lifecycle system.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: Map standard macOS Hide/Minimize/Mission Control behavior to GTK/window-manager conventions while preserving confirmation, activation, fullscreen and restored-placement outcomes.

entries.behavior: Expose stable/beta update availability, release notes, trusted install/upgrade and failure-safe rollback through Linux packaging rather than silently dropping the Sparkle-owned source outcome.
entries.user_impact: Users need a visible, trustworthy path to fixes without an in-app updater damaging or bypassing their Linux package ownership.
entries.test_plan: Use a controlled signed package/update repository to test stable/beta discovery, availability UI, success, invalid signature, interruption, offline, rollback and unchanged prior install; mutate state transitions.
entries.alternative_or_blocker: Integrate distribution/package update metadata and user-invoked package-manager upgrade rather than porting Sparkle; preserve channel, visibility, trust, release-note and rollback outcomes.

entries.behavior: Show build/version/commit metadata, docs/source and complete third-party licenses, provide local diagnostics, and enforce Zentty's no telemetry/analytics promise with crash transmission only after explicit user review and consent.
entries.user_impact: A public terminal handling agent content and tokens must disclose its build and dependencies and must never silently export user data.
entries.test_plan: About/build identity and the exact staged/installed license catalog are covered by controlled X11/Wayland product journeys, malformed-bundle recovery, Debian payload audit, installed-product execution, controlled link handlers, and focused mutation testing. Diagnostics default disabled and network-silent; opt-in real panic capture uses a bounded allowlist, private atomic XDG storage, retention and corruption recovery, complete local review, safe-default second confirmation, explicit controlled failure/retry/transmission, persisted sent/failed lifecycle, revocable capture, clearing, and hostile-secret redaction in the same controlled X11/Wayland product journey. The installed Debian product also remains silent behind a live capture origin through real multi-pane terminals, controlled agent hooks, settings, clipboard, persistence, injected failure, restart, About, Open With, CLI, and desktop-entry launch.

entries.behavior: Provide opt-in terminal performance overlay, frame/viewport diagnostics and bounded breadcrumbs/signposts that support troubleshooting without materially slowing terminals or exposing commands, output, paths, or tokens.
entries.user_impact: Source diagnostics are needed to investigate rendering and hang regressions, but must not introduce the performance or privacy failure they diagnose.
entries.test_plan: Run representative high-output real terminals with diagnostics off/on, bound overhead and storage, inspect/redact receipts, exercise overlay through the staged app, and mutation-test redaction and metric state.

entries.behavior: Discover agent launches, require integration consent, install or select the approved wrapper or hook, and preserve one-shot restore semantics.
entries.user_impact: Agent hooks must not be silently installed, while approved integrations must work consistently across new and restored panes.
entries.test_plan: Use real installed agent binaries where qualification owns them, staged managed wrappers/hooks and private files for every supported launcher, real shell/PTY/socket/consent paths, and control only the external model response.

entries.behavior: Receive real hook and wrapper events over the local IPC protocol, adapt them into pane status, progress, questions, and attention, and render those states.
entries.user_impact: Without the real event path, Zentty is merely a terminal multiplexer and cannot surface coding-agent progress or questions.
entries.test_plan: Run real terminal children, staged wrappers/hooks, authenticated Unix sockets, every implemented protocol adapter, the canonical reducer, persisted restore drafts, and sidebar/attention projection; control only the external agent response.

entries.behavior: Support Codex discovery, notify/transcript events, status resolution, questions and approvals, title promotion, write-back, and resume.
entries.user_impact: Codex is a primary supported coding workflow and must expose real progress and human-attention transitions.
entries.test_plan: Preserve the delivered real Codex CLI/PTY/hook/IPC/resume journey, complete hook and notify adapter, bounded real transcript question extraction including 12-candidate/four-day CWD-scoped discovery and cache identity, title-driven asynchronous retry/cache enrichment, real Ghostty OSC 9;4 progress reconciliation, transactional resolver-state write-back, and the installed Codex 0.147.0 completed-turn journey through the deterministic loopback Responses endpoint and Codex-originated notify callback. The write-back contract does not automatically rename panes: skipped title transitions discard local reducer mutations, while real transitions commit them.

entries.behavior: Animate the source Braille activity indicator for eligible live local Codex work without changing pane identity, title ownership, attention state, or inactive and restored presentation.
entries.user_impact: Without the activity treatment, running Codex panes lose the current source application's glanceable distinction between active work and static identity.
entries.test_plan: Separate stable display identity from frame presentation, unit-test eligibility and frame progression with an injected monotonic clock, and run a real controlled Codex event journey proving animation only while eligible, no topology or persisted-title mutation, immediate stop on terminal state change, and bounded repaint behavior while hidden or inactive.

entries.behavior: Support Claude Code hooks, session correlation, stop-race handling, explicit state, title presentation, questions, and resume.
entries.user_impact: Claude Code users otherwise lose hook-driven completion and attention state.
entries.test_plan: Exercise the real installed Claude hook command and team lifecycle, session store, Unix IPC, Ghostty PTYs, sidebar, stop-race reconciliation, tmux-compat routing, and validated resume with only the remote model response controlled.

entries.behavior: Provide Zentty's hand-rolled tmux compatibility facade for Claude Code agent teams: a bundled tmux shim and CLI route authenticated commands over the running app's Agent IPC socket into existing worklane, pane, layout, terminal-input, capture, and compatibility-store behavior without becoming a second PTY multiplexer.
entries.user_impact: Without the compatibility path, Claude Code agent teams cannot create and control their source-equivalent subordinate pane topology inside Zentty even when ordinary terminals and Claude hooks work.
entries.test_plan: Freeze the source command and alias contract, test Rust parsing/protocol/store logic and mutations, then drive the staged and installed tmux shim as a real subprocess through a private Unix socket into the real Zentty app, Ghostty surfaces, and PTYs. Cover the current bare `--` parser contract, exact detached/printed/formatted Claude `-- cat` deferred bootstrap, immediate ordinary commands, valid deferred compound respawn, rejection of live or stale targets, first-split golden geometry, later vertical stacking, leader focus, send/list/capture/select/kill, width restoration, concurrent wait-for clients, restart, corrupt state, permissions, authentication, malformed input, and oversized requests; control only the remote model response. In the existing staged product actor, create two real GTK windows with real Ghostty PTYs under private X11 and Wayland compositors, route separate CLI subprocesses through pane capabilities from both windows without changing the caller's active worklane or focus, reject cross-window explicit pane targets, keep selection and team anchors worklane-scoped, and prove buffers plus wait-for signals retain their source-defined application-instance scope.

entries.test_plan: Keep the staged wrapper, private merged system-settings overlay, complete hook mapping, authenticated sidebar approval state, Ghostty-decoded Action required/Session complete notifications, source-compatible resume command, controlled real model turn, and restored real Gemini TUI/sidebar evidence green under controlled X11 and input-capable Wayland.
